notes: TIER: robots.txt fetched via curl_cffi (chrome120 impersonation) since plain curl/WebFetch got 403 (Akamai bot-block); robots.txt explicitly Allow:/ for ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, Claude-User, Claude-SearchBot, anthropic-ai, so proceeded. Direct HTTP (curl_cffi) worked for SSR HTML/sitemaps but the Angular-Universal category pages only SSR a small (8-item) preview list with no total-count field in markup - product counts needed live rendering. Plain Playwright (bundled Chromium) was fully blocked by Akamai at the network level (Access Denied even with anti-automation flags), so per hard-block rule escalated to Claude-in-Chrome (tier 3, explicitly allowed by robots.txt), which loaded pages normally and exposed the sidebar facet counts and 'Showing X of Y options' totals used for qty. METHOD: (1) fetched /robots.txt and /sitemap/sitemap-index.xml -> found a dedicated /sitemap/festive_decor.xml sitemap (7 URLs) confirming Pepperfry has a formal 'Festive Decor' taxonomy node (breadcrumb Home > Home Decor > Festive Decor) with 7 named children: Diwali Celebrations, Christmas Decorations, Rangolis, Torans, Decorative Diyas, Urli, Tea Light and Candle Holders. (2) Rendered each child + the parent in Chrome to read the sidebar facet counts and 'Showing 1-40 of N options' totals (exact, site-displayed). (3) Also swept all other sitemaps (furniture/home_decor/lamps_and_lighting/kitchen_and_dining/furnishings/sofas_and_seating/luxury/mattresses/website) for holiday keywords (Diwali, Christmas, New Year, Holi, Navratri, Raksha Bandhan, Eid, Ganpati, Halloween, Easter, Valentine, Mother's/Father's Day, Thanksgiving); this surfaced ~30 '/discover/*' landing pages with holiday keywords in the URL/title (e.g. diwali-lights, diwali-lanterns, diwali-collections, diwali-candles, halloween-decoration, easter-decoration, valentine-gifts, new-year-decorations, mothers-day-sale, fathers-day-sale/gifts, ganpati-decoration/sale, holi-sale, eid-offers, dhanteras-diwali-essentials, christmas-2025, new-year-2026, metal/plastic-festive-decor, etc). Rendered a representative sample of these in Chrome and found they are NOT genuine seasonal categories: several (halloween-decoration.html, easter-decoration.html, diwali-candles.html) all resolved to the exact same generic 'Candles' catalog subset (identical product list/count, zero holiday-themed products - e.g. 'Halloween Decoration' page contained only plain scented/pillar candles, no Halloween items at all); others (valentine-gifts.html, diwali-collections.html, new-year-decorations.html) resolved to the ENTIRE Furniture or Home Decor catalog (11,000-16,000+ items) under a discount-campaign title ('Pepperfry Sale 2025', 'Limited Time Offer: Buy Upto 60% Off') - a storewide-sale wrapper, explicitly excluded by the boundary rules. diwali-lights.html and diwali-lanterns.html looked more promising (distinct breadcrumb nodes under Lamps and Lighting) but their product grids were generic decorative-lights/table-lamps assortments with no Diwali-specific curation (irrelevant items like a laser-pointer keychain torch and a 'Kiss Couple' showpiece), and metal-festive-decor.html/plastic-festive-decor.html turned out to be material-attribute cross-filters over the SAME products already counted in the formal Festive Decor children (would double-count) - all were excluded as non-genuine/duplicative. ganpati-decoration.html, dhanteras-diwali-essentials.html, fathers-day-gifts.html and diwali-gifts.html returned only the generic homepage shell (dead/removed discover pages). No dedicated Ganpati/Ganesh Chaturthi, Holi, Navratri, Raksha Bandhan, Eid, New Year, Thanksgiving, or Mother's/Father's Day CATEGORY (as opposed to fake discover page) exists anywhere in the sitemap-listed taxonomy - checked thoroughly given the Indian-market expectation, confirmed absent beyond the sale-wrapper pages. INCLUDED ROWS (from the genuine /category/ 'Festive Decor' taxonomy, each verified with its own breadcrumb, its own sidebar facet count, and (for the 4 generic-named ones) extensive unique on-page copy explicitly tying the products to Diwali - distinguishing them from the fake /discover/ pages which had zero holiday-specific copy or products): Festive Decor (parent grouping row, is_group true, not counted toward any holiday total itself); Diwali Celebrations (explicitly named, 90); Rangolis (6) - page copy: 'known to be of great significance in Hindu festivals such as Diwali'; Torans (104) - FAQ explicitly says 'buy a new toran every Diwali', multiple product titles say 'for Diwali'/'Diwali Festival Decor'; Decorative Diyas (25) - contains multiple 'Diwali Gift Hamper' SKUs; Urli (134) - contains a SKU explicitly titled '...Diwali Decoration Items Gifts...'; Christmas Decorations (explicitly named, 49, copy and products - Nativity Crib Set, X-Mas Tree cushion cover - are genuinely Christmas-specific). EXCLUDED: Tea Light and Candle Holders (515, formally a Festive Decor child but a generic year-round home-decor product type with no distinguishing holiday-specific copy/products, unlike the other 4); Festive Lights (77, under Lamps and Lighting > Decorative Lights, explicitly multi-occasion per its own copy: 'Whether it's Diwali, Eid, New Year, Navroz, birthdays, anniversaries'); all ~30 /discover/ holiday-keyword pages (fake SEO wrappers over generic Candles/Furniture/Home-Decor/Decorative-Lights catalogs, several literally identical to each other across different holiday titles, or storewide sale campaigns, or dead pages). Mother's Day / Father's Day were checked (mothers-day-sale.html, fathers-day-sale.html, fathers-day-gifts.html) and are only generic sale-wrapper or dead pages - no genuine PLP found, so excluded on the same PLP-genuineness grounds as Halloween/Easter/Valentine, not on 'universal occasion' grounds. All qty figures are the exact 'Showing X of Y options' / sidebar facet counts rendered live in the browser on 2026-09-04 (site's own 'last updated 2026/09/03' timestamp shown on pages).
